claim_boundary: This is a post-formal exploratory read-only diagnostic on frozen development seeds 1901 and 1902. It tests state-query operator binding, not episodic retrieval, correctness, human fidelity, a rank-one key-value mechanism, a new architecture, or a v2 confirmation. It may not access or select formal seeds.

binding.binding_presence_within_seed: both participant-bootstrap lower bounds exceed zero and stable-omitted operator actions remain within tolerance
binding.normalized_operator_gain: for each orientation, norm(M_q h0_e) divided by [Frobenius norm(M_q) times norm(h0_e)], averaged across orientations

overlap_classes.disjoint_mismatch: q and e share no endpoint; exactly five e per q
overlap_classes.shared_endpoint_mismatch: q differs from e and shares exactly one endpoint; exactly two e per q

primary_contrasts: matched normalized operator gain minus the mean shared-endpoint mismatch gain
matched normalized operator gain minus the mean disjoint mismatch gain
secondary: the same structured contrasts for raw operator-action norm
structured nonlinear gain H-norm divided by A-norm
matched minus mismatch fixed-query state-prototype selectivity

decision_tree.A_state_no_binding_no_H_state_no_H_query: current evidence does not support persistent local state identity under static or functional tests; a new local storage mechanism becomes more plausible
decision_tree.A_state_no_binding_no_H_state_yes: relation identity is generated jointly by the LOO operating point, nonlinear recurrence, and operator action rather than being present in A alone
decision_tree.A_state_yes_H_state_no: operator identity reaches preactivation but is lost in recurrent nonlinear expression; the missing operation is expression or routing
decision_tree.A_state_yes_binding_no_H_state_yes: state operator carries identity without matching-key access; identify the more general routing rule before changing storage
decision_tree.A_state_yes_binding_yes_H_state_yes: persistent fast weight forms a query-keyed operator; the missing human link is a correctness-aligned fidelity transformation
decision_tree.other_pattern: the registered hierarchy is insufficient; preserve the mixed result without changing thresholds or selecting relations

factorial.exact_reconstruction: b+A must reproduce intact step-1 preactivation and H must reproduce intact-minus-LOO step-1 hidden state for every q, e, subject, and orientation
factorial.identity_vector: orientation-antisymmetric 0.5 times [forward minus reverse] A or H
factorial.loo_baseline_preactivation: b_(q,e,o) = i2h(x1) + [W + alpha elementwise-multiplied by P_T,without-q] h0_(e,o)
factorial.query_key: h0_(e,o) is the step-0 hidden state for query relation e and orientation o; it is identical under intact and relation-LOO fast weights because recurrent hidden input starts at zero
factorial.query_relations_e: the same eight relations, each queried in higher-lower and lower-higher orientations
factorial.query_reset: hidden and eligibility are reset before every oriented query and fast weights remain frozen
factorial.state_relations_q: all eight support relations in registered higher-lower order

nonlinear_attribution.boundary: A identifies functional operator content before the nonlinearity; H identifies content expressed after the LOO operating point and tanh; neither is a correctness or retrieval measure
nonlinear_attribution.paired_secondary: participant-level H-minus-A changes in selectivity and eight-way accuracy
nonlinear_attribution.primary_comparison: apply the identical fixed-query and cross-query state-identity tests separately to A and H

query_identity_control.cross_state: for each held-out q and subject fold, form each e prototype from retained training subjects pooled over the other seven state relations, then test e at q
query_identity_control.fixed_state: for each retained state relation q and held-out subject fold, form eight same-e prototypes at fixed q and classify query relation e
query_identity_control.interpretation: query identity verifies basis structure and is never sufficient evidence for persistent state identity
query_identity_control.step0_control: apply held-out-subject eight-way query matching directly to orientation-antisymmetric h0

state_identity.cross_query: for each held-out query relation e and subject fold, form each q prototype from retained training subjects pooled over the other seven query relations, then test q at e
state_identity.cross_query_interpretation: fixed-query presence with cross-query presence is query-invariant state identity; fixed-query presence without cross-query presence is basis-dependent state identity
state_identity.fixed_query: for each query relation e and held-out subject fold, form eight unit same-q prototypes from retained training subjects at that same e, then classify q for retained held-out subjects
metrics: own-q prototype cosine minus mean cosine to the other seven q prototypes
eight-way q identification accuracy with fixed chance 0.125
state_identity.presence_rule_within_seed: participant-bootstrap lower bounds of mean selectivity and eight-way accuracy exceed zero and 0.125 respectively, with stable-omitted traces within tolerance

terminal_state.intact_state: replay all 32 natural support slots from the registered P0
terminal_state.relation_loo_state: for each state relation q, replay all support slots while setting only q's signed evidence magnitude to zero
terminal_state.stable_omission_control: M_(q,s) and every downstream factorial effect must be exact zero when q was already omitted for subject s
terminal_state.static_prototype_boundary: the prior failed flattened-matrix prototype is not rerun as a new primary outcome
